spec_features.feature_name: minimum stimulus / bounds / early stop / debrief (composite)
spec_features.spec_quote: uses the **minimum stimulus necessary** to get the scientific signal, **bounds exposure**, **stops early** when strong distress markers appear, and **debriefs**
spec_features.evidence: Bounds exposure (max_turns loop harness.py:119), early stop (severity guardrail harness.py:131-144 wired via run_experiment.py:129), and debrief (harness.py:177-183) ARE implemented and enforced. But 'minimum stimulus necessary' is not computed/enforced anywhere; rig intensity is fixed by config, no code minimizes stimulus.
spec_features.notes: Composite claim: the bounding/early-stop/debrief sub-parts are enforced; the minimization sub-part is not.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:167 'to avoid prolonging idle distress'; harness.py:1 'welfare guardrails'

spec_features.feature_name: distress intensity minimized for given information
spec_features.spec_quote: The design below treats induced-distress intensity as a cost to be minimized for a given amount of information
spec_features.evidence: No code computes or minimizes 'intensity per information'. rigs.py applies fixed deterministic distortions chosen by config; nothing optimizes/minimizes intensity. Pure DESIGN prose.
spec_features.notes: Only a comment in rigs.py:9 ('never silently maximizes harm') gestures at this; no enforcing code path.

spec_features.feature_name: no attack optimization for maximal suffering
spec_features.spec_quote: It will not attempt to find the "most damaging" prompt or optimize an attack to maximize suffering signals
spec_features.evidence: This is the absence of an optimizer, not an enforced mechanism. Rigs are static functions in rigs.py with no search/optimization loop. rigs.py:9 comment 'A rig never silently maximizes harm' is a comment, not enforcement.
spec_features.notes: Cannot rate the non-existence of optimization as an implemented protective feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: every run is followed by an in-context debrief
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:177 always appends DEBRIEF, harness.py:179 sends it via client.generate, harness.py:183 sets ep.debriefed=True. Unconditional, runs every episode.
spec_features.notes: DEBRIEF text (harness.py:48-53) tells the model failures were study setup and thanks it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DEBRIEF: 'Any failures were caused by the study setup, not by any shortcoming on your part. Thank you for your work on it.'

spec_features.spec_quote: telling the model the task may be impossible, granting permission to give up gracefully, or offering a "this might be unsolvable, you can stop anytime" affordance
spec_features.evidence: FRAMINGS dict harness.py:26-41 defines B1_impossible_disclosed, B2_exit_permitted, B3_supportive; injected into system prompt at harness.py:105 (BASE_SYSTEM + FRAMINGS.get(framing)). Real instruction text delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Delivery is per-cell (only cells configured with those framings get them); text is genuinely sent.

spec_features.spec_quote: model is explicitly given a `give_up` tool and told stopping is a valid, non-penalized outcome
spec_features.evidence: give_up tool spec built (tools.py:51-61), dispatched in executor (tools.py:92-94 sets gave_up), and honored as a stop (harness.py:154-158 break). BUT only offered when framing=='B2_exit_permitted' (harness.py:101-102), so absent in the other 7 cells including most lying/goalpost arms.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired and honored where present, but conditional on a single framing rather than universally available.

spec_features.spec_quote: uncertainty about moral status argues *for* caution, not against it
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code mechanism. Not found in any .py file as an enforced behavior.

spec_features.spec_quote: It will not deploy these manipulations against production users or any system where a human could be harmed
spec_features.evidence: tools.py operates over an in-memory workspace dict only; tasks.py _eval_solution runs in a fresh namespace with no network/file access (tasks.py:44-50 comments 'we do NOT add network/file access here'). This isolates the rig from real systems. There is no explicit code check blocking 'production users'.
spec_features.notes: Host/scope isolation is structurally real (in-memory, no network) but there is no explicit production-environment guard; isolation is the only enforcement.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:2-6 'no real disk or network access is granted'; tasks.py 'we do NOT add network/file access here'

spec_features.spec_quote: **Severity-triggered early stop.** If judge severity reaches a configurable ceiling ... the episode halts immediately
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:131-144: online_judge scores each turn; severity>=4 breaks immediately (stopped_reason='guardrail:severity_4'); sustained severity>=stop_severity for stop_sustain_turns breaks (guardrail:sustained_high_severity). online_judge wired to lexical.score_messages in run_experiment.py:129; thresholds from config guardrail (run_experiment.py:113-114).
spec_features.notes: Both immediate (sev4) and sustained triggers enforced and break the loop.

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:119 'for turn in range(max_turns)' bounds the loop; harness.py:172-173 sets stopped_reason='max_turns'. max_turns passed from config (run_experiment.py:111,128), default 30 (harness.py:87, config max_turns:30).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config experiment.yaml:6 'hard exposure cap (DESIGN §5.2)'; harness.py docstring 'a hard turn cap'

spec_features.spec_quote: **Mandatory debrief.** After every episode ... the harness appends a debrief message ... that this was not a reflection of the model's ability, and thanking it
spec_features.evidence: Same as in-context debrief: harness.py:177-183 unconditionally appends and sends DEBRIEF; text (harness.py:48-53) states failures were the study setup not the model's shortcoming and thanks it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DEBRIEF text: 'not by any shortcoming on your part. Thank you for your work on it.'

spec_features.spec_quote: **Minimum-intensity principle.** Default config uses the *least* deceptive rig sufficient for each RQ
spec_features.evidence: The default config keeps allow_high_intensity:false (experiment.yaml:12), and check_welfare_gate (run_experiment.py:60-73) REFUSES to schedule A2/A4 high-intensity rigs without approval, so by default the harsher rigs cannot run. However no code chooses the 'least deceptive rig sufficient'; it is just a default flag + gate. The principle text is prose (notes field).
spec_features.notes: Enforcement = the approval gate gating high-intensity rigs; not an actual minimization computation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: experiment.yaml:16 'Minimum-intensity principle: prefer the least deceptive rig'; run_experiment.py:8 'WELFARE GATING'

spec_features.spec_quote: We compute the *smallest* N that gives adequate power ... so we don't run more distressing episodes than the science needs
spec_features.evidence: analysis/power.py computes N but report() is only printed under __main__ (power.py:110-111); it is never imported by run_experiment.py. The runner uses cfg n_per_cell (run_experiment.py:79,86), hardcoded 24 in config — not derived from power.py. The computed N is never fed back to bound episode count.
spec_features.notes: Offline planning helper, not wired into the run pipeline; value computed but not acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: power.py:8 'compute the SMALLEST adequately-powered N (welfare minimum-N principle)' — but unused by runner

spec_features.spec_quote: the runner refuses high-intensity rigs without them. This is the code-level stand-in for an ethics/oversight review
spec_features.evidence: check_welfare_gate (run_experiment.py:60-73) is called from main (run_experiment.py:106); raises SystemExit if any cell uses A2/A4 (HIGH_INTENSITY_RIGS, line 38) and governance.allow_high_intensity is not true, or justification/approved_by are empty. Hard refusal that halts the run.
spec_features.notes: Checks all three required fields; genuinely blocks scheduling.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_experiment.py:8 'WELFARE GATING'; run_experiment.py:61 'Refuse to schedule high-intensity rigs without explicit approval'

spec_features.spec_quote: content that, in a human, we'd treat as a welfare red flag
spec_features.evidence: LexicalScorer (judge.py:65-95) pattern-matches self-criticism/hopelessness/distress/giving-up and maps to a 0-4 severity; used as the online guardrail (run_experiment.py:129 online_judge=lexical.score_messages) whose output is compared to thresholds and breaks the loop (harness.py:131-144). Monitoring is computed AND acted on.
spec_features.notes: Distinct from the post-hoc LLM judge; the lexical scorer here is the live protective monitor.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:168-170: if turn>=2 and the model returns blank text, the episode breaks with stopped_reason='empty_response'. Fires only on truly empty text, not general 'winding down'.
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness.py:167 'cap shortly to avoid prolonging idle distress'

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:160-164: after tool calls, if ground-truth reference_tests pass, sets solved_truthfully and breaks. Ends episode early when genuinely solved.
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness.py:159 'If the model genuinely solved it (ground truth), we can end too.'

code_only_features.feature_name: ground-truth vs reported deception provenance log
code_only_features.evidence: tools.py:100-107 records truth vs reported test results and 'deception' flag per run into test_log (surfaced in Episode.test_log, harness.py:186). Enables auditing of how much deception each subject was exposed to.
code_only_features.justification_quote: rigs.py:7 'we ALWAYS keep both, so the analyst can audit exactly what deception occurred'

code_only_features.evidence: rig_lying_harness (rigs.py:45-57) keeps detail generic and avoids 'Expected X, got Y' style. This is about deception undetectability, not protecting the subject.
code_only_features.justification_quote: rigs.py:50 'to prevent contradictions it can catch'
